text:
maria: Heads up — since ~13:12 UTC we're seeing intermittent DNS failures from edge-east -> internal model-svc (redwood-models.private). ~5% of requests get NXDOMAIN or 10s resolution delays, then envoy upstream connect errors. Started after Friday's NAT egress tweak.

aj: Oof. Can you paste /etc/resolv.conf and the kube node-local-dns logs? Also which NAT change was rolled?

maria: /etc/resolv.conf on an affected node:

```
# Generated by NetworkManager
search redwood.internal svc.cluster.local cluster.local
nameserver 10.2.0.10
nameserver 8.8.8.8
options ndots:5 timeout:2 rotate
```

node-local-dns seems up, but logs show a bunch of "SERVFAIL" responses forwarded to 8.8.8.8.

kenji: Two quick hypotheses: 1) Split-horizon: internal resolver view depends on client SNAT IP. If our NAT change introduced two egress IPs, some DNS queries may be forwarded to upstream resolvers that don't see the internal CIDR and return NXDOMAIN. 2) Resolver caching + short TTLs + multipath egress -> inconsistent answers.

aj: Confirming — Friday change added a second NAT gateway for edge-east to improve throughput, sessions are round-robin hashed across them. That would give at least two different external IPs. If the authoritative DNS for redwood-models.private uses ACLs or view-based answers, that explains it.

jen: Temporary mitigation: route DNS (port 53) traffic from nodes to a single NAT IP or force use of our internal forwarder IP only (10.2.0.10) and avoid 8.8.8.8. Also increase ndots? Not necessary here.

maria: Quick test: I forced one node to use only 10.2.0.10 and restarted kube-dns — resolution stabilized for that node. Rolling that change cluster-wide reduced error rate to ~0.2%.

kenji: Actions I recommend:
- Revert multipath behavior for UDP/53 (pin DNS flows to single egress IP) OR
- Ensure both NAT gateways present the same view to upstream (e.g., they forward to same internal DNS forwarders with consistent zone views) OR
- Make node-local-dns authoritative for cluster-internal zones so external views don't matter.

aj: For short-term rollback I've created a route policy to SNAT DNS -> nat-east-1a (single IP). Rolling now.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Route update applied to edge-east (rollout id: r-2026-03-14-42).

maria: After SNAT pin, error rate back to baseline. Thanks.

jen: Follow-ups for next week:
- Add e2e test that queries internal zones from multiple egress IPs to catch view mismatches.
- Document that authoritative split-horizon zones must be visible to all NAT egress IPs or we must preserve client SNAT.
- Consider adding an explicit DNS egress path: all 53/UDP -> a managed resolver pair with HA.

kenji: Also: watch for caching effects. If some upstream caches had negative answers cached, we need TTL expiry. For immediate cache flushes: sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches (on nodes) and restart node-local-dns.

maria: I'll follow up with a short postmortem and link to the NAT change PR. TL;DR: DNS split-horizon + multipath SNAT = intermittent NXDOMAIN; fixed by pinning DNS SNAT to single egress IP.

aj: Great job triaging — keep the rollback until we implement a long-term fix. :thumbsup:
